title: Google Invests Over $1.5 Billion to Acquire Mechanize AI, Fueling Competition in the Programming Field
excerpt: Google is in discussions with the San Francisco startup Mechanize about a potential deal worth over $1.5 billion, involving talent acquisition and technology li
content_html:
Google is in discussions with the San Francisco startup Mechanize about a potential deal worth over $1.5 billion, involving talent acquisition and technology licensing. According to informed sources, Google may obtain Mechanize's AI programming technology through a non-exclusive license, while also bringing in its core talent to work on model evaluation and development. This deal highlights that programming has become one of the most critical and profitable applications in the AI field, with tech giants vying aggressively for related talent and technology.

Mechanize was founded last year, with CEO Tamay Besiroglu co-founding Epoch AI, a company focused on AI model testing. The company recently secured a $9.1 million funding round, valuing it at $500 million. Its investor list includes former GitHub CEO Nat Friedman, Stripe CEO Patrick Collison, and popular podcaster Dwarkesh Patel. Its technology helps tech companies improve the coding performance of AI models, which is a key area where Google currently needs improvement—OpenAI's Codex and Anthropic's Claude Code have already captured a large number of developer users.

Hybrid Deal Models Have Become Google's Common Strategy

This is not the first time Google has used an unconventional way to acquire talent and technology. In recent years, Google has repeatedly used a "acquisition-style hiring plus technology licensing" hybrid deal model, allowing it to quickly absorb key talent while avoiding antitrust scrutiny associated with full acquisitions. When OpenAI attempted to acquire Windsurf last year, Google swiftly moved in to hire its talent and obtain a technology license. Windsurf CEO Varun Mohan now leads Google's intelligent agent coding platform Antigravity.

Similar moves include rehiring Character AI co-founder Noam Shazeer in 2024 and obtaining non-exclusive rights to his technology, although Shazeer later moved to OpenAI. Mechanize's ambitions go far beyond programming; its website clearly states that its long-term goal is to achieve full automation of all high-value jobs in the economy. If the deal is finalized, Google will gain a significant advantage in the AI programming space, making competition with OpenAI and Anthropic even fiercer.

content_html_zh:
Google 正在与旧金山初创公司 Mechanize 讨论一项价值超过 15 亿美元的潜在交易，涉及人才收购和技术许可。 据知情人士透露，谷歌可能会通过非独家许可的方式获得Mechanize的AI编程技术，同时也会引入其核心人才进行模型评估和开发。 这笔交易凸显出编程已成为人工智能领域最关键和最有利可图的应用之一，科技巨头们正在积极争夺相关人才和技术。

Mechanize 于去年成立，首席执行官 Tamay Besiroglu 联合创立了 Epoch AI，这是一家专注于人工智能模型测试的公司。 该公司最近获得了 910 万美元的融资，估值达 5 亿美元。 其投资者名单包括 GitHub 前首席执行官纳特·弗里德曼 (Nat Friedman)、Stripe 首席执行官帕特里克·科里森 (Patrick Collison) 和受欢迎的播客德瓦克什·帕特尔 (Dwarkesh Patel)。 其技术帮助科技公司提高AI模型的编码性能，这是谷歌目前需要改进的关键领域——OpenAI的Codex和Anthropic的Claude Code已经俘获了大量的开发者用户。

混合交易模式已成为谷歌的共同策略

这并不是谷歌第一次使用非常规方式获取人才和技术。 近年来，谷歌多次采用“收购式招聘加技术许可”的混合交易模式，使其能够快速吸收关键人才，同时避免与全面收购相关的反垄断审查。 去年，当 OpenAI 试图收购 Windsurf 时，谷歌迅速介入，聘请其人才并获得技术许可。 Windsurf 首席执行官 Varun Mohan 现在领导 Google 的智能代理编码平台 Antigravity。

类似的举措包括在 2024 年重新雇用 Character AI 联合创始人 Noam Shazeer 并获得其技术的非独家权利，尽管 Shazeer 后来转到了 OpenAI。 Mechanize 的野心远远超出了编程范畴。其网站明确指出，其长期目标是实现经济中所有高价值工作的全面自动化。 如果交易最终完成，谷歌将在人工智能编程领域获得显着优势，使得与 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的竞争更加激烈。
